summary: Spark-only prototype rules passed emulator authorization tests. Owner-private records are isolated; exact approved redacted snapshots allow only UUID get, never public list. Expiry, revocation and revisions are enforced in rules; strict per-read counting is impossible in this direct-client architecture.

findings.issue: Bearer can read a permitted snapshot without incrementing; can consume counts without viewing.
findings.recommendation: Treat counts as app-level access limits; strict accounting requires a trusted gateway outside Spark-only Firebase.

findings.issue: Preserved VITE_GROQ_API_KEY is public in browser output.
findings.recommendation: Secure secret handling needs an external backend/proxy; no paid Firebase backend added.

findings.issue: Private draft/profile nested content is flexible and not bounded at every leaf.
findings.recommendation: Version and bound owner schemas while preserving actual supported fields.

findings.issue: Download flags and revocation cannot prevent copying or erase prior deliveries.
findings.recommendation: Keep policy explicit; do not promise DRM.

tested: Resume-only and combined atomic redacted snapshot creation
Public metadata changes and snapshot updates denied
Concurrent app redemption permits one final view
Public portfolio publish and private-state invalidation
Known direct-read counting bypass reproduced and disclosed
